title: The C*-algebra generated by the CAR representation and the shell unitaries

content.display_title: The C*-algebra generated by the CAR representation and the shell unitaries
content.one_sentence_role: Defines the single algebra $T$ used in the irreducible and separable faithful representations.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra and let $\omega$ be its distinguished pure state. Let $I$ be the set of unitary-equivalence classes of pure-state GNS representations. Choose a representative $\pi_i:A\to B(H_i)$ in each class, keeping the GNS representation of $\omega$ in its distinguished class, and put $\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i\in I}H_i$ and $\pi=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\pi_i$. Fix the automorphisms and shell partial isometries supplied by CAR homogeneity, and choose the corresponding unitaries $L_i$ on $\mathcal H$ by the cited shell construction. Define $$T=C^*\bigl(\pi(A)\cup\{L_i:i\in I\}\bigr)\subseteq B(\mathcal H).$$
content.definition_explanation: $T$ is the norm-closed unital complex $*$-subalgebra of $B(\mathcal H)$ generated by $\pi(A)$ and the unitaries $L_i$. The automorphisms, shell partial isometries and resulting unitaries are chosen once; the abbreviation does not choose another isomorphic copy of the algebra.
content.assumptions: The CAR algebra, the pure state $\omega$, the GNS representatives and the unitaries $L_i$ are those in the cited fixed construction. The index set $I$ is not assumed countable.
content.conclusion: The notation $T$ refers to this particular generated C*-algebra. It does not denote a new isomorphic copy when different representations of $T$ are considered.
content.lean_realization_notes: The abbreviation defines the algebra; separate theorems establish its simplicity, uniqueness of the nonzero irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence, and failure to be isomorphic to an algebra of compact operators. The fixed construction uses the proved CAR homogeneity theorem, without an additional KOS or CH hypothesis.
